questionText:
Consider the relation $R(P, Q, S, T, X, Y, Z, W)$ with the following functional dependencies.

$$PQ \rightarrow X; \quad P \rightarrow YX; \quad Q \rightarrow Y; \quad Y \rightarrow ZW$$

Consider the decomposition of the relation $R$ into the constituent relations according to the following two decomposition schemes.

$$D_1 : \quad R = [(P, Q, S, T); (P, T, X); (Q, Y); (Y, Z, W)]$$
$$D_2 : \quad R = [(P, Q, S); (T, X); (Q, Y); (Y, Z, W)]$$

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: $D_1$ is a lossless decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossy decomposition.
$D_1$ is a lossy decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossless decomposition.
explanation:
To determine whether decompositions $D_1$ and $D_2$ are lossless or lossy, we apply the Chase algorithm/attribute closure testing.

Testing Scheme $D_1$:
The decomposed relations are $R_1(P, Q, S, T)$, $R_2(P, T, X)$, $R_3(Q, Y)$, and $R_4(Y, Z, W)$.
1. Using $Y \rightarrow ZW$: Since $R_4$ contains $Y, Z, W$ and $R_3$ contains $Y$, $R_3$ gains attributes $Z$ and $W$.
2. Using $Q \rightarrow Y$: Since $R_3$ contains $Q, Y, Z, W$ and $R_1$ contains $Q$, $R_1$ gains attributes $Y, Z, W$.
3. Using $P \rightarrow YX$: Since $R_2$ contains $P, X$ and $R_1$ contains $P$, $R_1$ gains attribute $X$.
Thus, $R_1$ contains all attributes $(P, Q, S, T, X, Y, Z, W)$, proving that $D_1$ is a lossless decomposition.

Testing Scheme $D_2$:
The decomposed relations are $R_1(P, Q, S)$, $R_2(T, X)$, $R_3(Q, Y)$, and $R_4(Y, Z, W)$.
1. Attribute $T$ appears only in $R_2(T, X)$.
2. No functional dependency has $T$ on the right-hand side, nor does $X$ determine $T$.
3. Consequently, $T$ cannot be propagated to any other relation, nor can $R_2$ gain the remaining attributes.
Therefore, $D_2$ is a lossy decomposition.

Hence, $D_1$ is lossless and $D_2$ is lossy.
